stories.Headline: Goldman Sachs Expert Call Warns: DRAM Shortage Could Last Until 2028, HBM Average Prices Seen Rising 122% Next Year
stories.Summary:
Goldman Sachs hosted a memory industry expert call on October 27, 2026, with research firm TrendForce taking part and sharing its latest forecasts. According to those forecasts, tight DRAM supply is expected to persist throughout 2027, with the price upcycle potentially reaching into the first half of 2028. High-bandwidth memory, or HBM, faces even steeper gains. Blended average prices are projected to rise 122% year over year in 2027 to $3.7 per gigabit, pushing total HBM industry revenue past $200 billion.

The main constraints on supply are insufficient cleanroom space and long lead times for semiconductor equipment. Memory makers are planning aggressive capital spending, but those two bottlenecks make meaningful new supply unlikely before 2028. Pricing will vary sharply by product, with HBM4 high-end pricing possibly above $5 per gigabit and low-end pricing near $3. HBM4 is expected to account for nearly 60% of HBM revenue in 2027. Long-term agreements covering 60% to 70% of volume could moderate increases in 2027, though suppliers can still negotiate higher prices for demand beyond contracted volumes.

Goldman Sachs and TrendForce present these views as their own estimates, with TrendForce noting that suppliers may manage the pace of capacity expansion based on their demand outlook. TrendForce also expects Google's growing deployment of its TPU chips to keep demand for HBM3E alive into 2027, spreading HBM demand across generations. Chinese suppliers are estimated to hold less than 2% of the market in 2027, and TrendForce says their gaps in technology and yield limit their near-term threat. Goldman Sachs reiterated Buy ratings on Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, with 12-month price targets of ₩500,000 and ₩3.5 million, respectively.

The bank also listed risks to this outlook. A sharper deterioration in memory supply and demand, weaker smartphone and PC demand, and slower technology migration could each hurt the companies involved. A pullback in AI-related capital spending would be especially damaging to HBM demand. Goldman Sachs also warned that more aggressive HBM progress by Samsung could squeeze SK Hynix's HBM revenue and profit. The articles describe the outlook as an upcycle that could last at least through the first half of 2028, with the actual benefit to each company depending on product mix, contract coverage, and the pace of AI spending.

Articles.Title: Goldman Sachs Expert Call Warns: DRAM Shortage Could Last Until 2028, HBM Average Prices Seen Rising 122% Next Year - BigGo Finance

stories.Headline: Renuity builds a governed AI platform on Azure and lifts sales conversion in pilot
stories.Summary:
Renuity, a full-service home remodeling business operating across 40 states, has built a governed AI platform on Microsoft Azure, according to a Microsoft customer story published on October 30, 2026. The company had been held back by fragmented systems, inconsistent data models, and technical debt left over from acquisitions, which made it hard to innovate with AI or trust the data behind it. Renuity chose Azure as an integrated, governed data plane, with Azure Machine Learning and Microsoft Foundry handling AI development and operations, and it plans to use Microsoft Fabric as the unified data layer. The platform is meant to give new AI projects a repeatable foundation so they can be delivered in weeks rather than months.

The platform standardizes infrastructure through infrastructure as code and selected Azure services, including managed identities, Microsoft Entra ID access, private networking, and policy enforcement. Governance covering data lineage, feedback loops, testing, and productionization is also standardized. Renuity identified 40 business use cases for AI and scored them on ROI, business impact, efficiency gains, partner engagement, and data readiness. The first pilots focused on the Renuity East contact center, where a new lead-scoring model called Project LQS produced a significant uplift in net-sales-per-raw-lead conversion in an A/B test. A second project, Project ACE, automated daily lead assignment, cutting the task from about three and a half hours to roughly 20 minutes.

Mayank Rathi, Renuity's Chief Technology Officer, said that the platform stopped being an IT initiative and became a business enabler once the lead-scoring results showed up, and he argued that a platform yields compounding returns while a single proof of concept yields a one-time gain. Liping Wu, Senior Director for Data Science and AI, described the approach as building shared infrastructure ahead of time so the AI team can focus on solutions rather than setup. Justin Rosenblum, Chief of Staff, reported the conversion results from the pilot, and Herculano Fernandes, Call Center Vice President, said the time saved now goes to coaching and evaluating staff. The article says the call center team is next exploring agentic, next-best-action orchestration, with people kept in the loop for critical decisions.

Articles.Title: Renuity builds a governed AI platform on Azure and lifts sales conversion in pilot

stories.Headline: Taiwan Semiconductor Said to Weigh 20% CoWoS Price Hike; Taiwan Index Futures Night Session Surges 774 Points as Investment Trusts Buy for 11th Straight Day
stories.Summary:
Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing's American depositary receipts climbed nearly 3% after Wall Street's Philadelphia Semiconductor Index jumped 3.6% in a single session, pushing the Taiwan Index Futures night session up 774 points. Market talk also emerged that the chipmaker is weighing a new round of price increases for its advanced CoWoS packaging. The reports were circulating on October 28, 2026, and came after days of choppy trading in Taiwan stocks. The rally offered a lift to bullish investors who had been battered by recent swings.

The talk centers on increases of 10% to 20% for CoWoS quotes, a packaging service described as in extreme shortage relative to demand. Industry sources said the chipmaker and its packaging and testing partners are preparing the adjustments, and some major international technology companies reportedly are willing to pay more to secure delivery schedules. Analysts estimate monthly CoWoS capacity could exceed 130,000 wafers in 2026 and challenge 200,000 wafers in 2027. Market participants cautioned that the figures come from industry sources and analysts, not from the company, so the actual scope and details have yet to be finalized.

Taiwan stocks extended their gains after the open on the 28th. By 9:33 a.m., the weighted index stood at 46,839.96, up 743.73 points or 1.61%, with turnover of about NT$244.375 billion. Taiwan Semiconductor shares traded at NT$2,425, up NT$25 or 1.04%. Investment trusts bought a net NT$23.645 billion in a single day, their 11th straight session of net buying, bringing the cumulative total to NT$179.969 billion (approximately $5.5 billion). Financial commentator Yeh Yu-shuo attributed much of that buying to Taiwanese investors subscribing to Taiwan stock ETFs through monthly plans and lump-sum purchases.

Institutional investors said the durability of domestic buying will be a key indicator of whether the rebound can continue, and they are watching whether foreign investors switch from selling to buying. Long-term demand is also being supported by heavy capital spending from large technology companies, with Meta expecting $135 billion to $145 billion in capital expenditure this year and Anthropic deepening a partnership with Broadcom worth as much as $161.2 billion. This week's focus includes earnings from Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon and the outcome of the Federal Reserve's rate-setting meeting. The articles note that if the price increases are confirmed, they would add to the chipmaker's margin improvement, while higher packaging costs could affect downstream chip designers and cloud providers.

Articles.Title: Taiwan Semiconductor Said to Weigh 20% CoWoS Price Hike; Taiwan Index Futures Night Session Surges 774 Points as Investment Trusts Buy for 11th Straight Day - BigGo Finance

stories.Headline: SK AX Launches AI Tool That Screened 1,800 Applicants in Six Hours
stories.Summary:
SK AX said on October 29, 2026 that it had launched G-Fit Studio, an artificial intelligence tool that assesses job applicants on their problem-solving, communication and AI skills. The company said it used the tool to screen about 1,800 applicants in six hours while selecting the fourth cohort of its SKALA talent development program, which is tied to employment. The report was published by Seoul Economic Daily, with reporting by Kim Ji-young. The tool works in two stages. In the first, applicants form a hypothesis about a given business situation, structure the problem through dialogue with an AI agent, and draw up an action plan, with the system recording the questions they ask and how they use the information.

In the second, applicants face a 30-minute in-depth interview based on their cover letter and their proposed solution, with the AI playing roles such as a human resources manager or a line department head. The solution can be adjusted to each company's job functions, gives all applicants the same tasks and criteria, and supports languages including English and Japanese. SK AX presented the product as a way to cut time and operational burden compared with conventional hiring, since the AI can interview several applicants at once. The company also said G-Fit Studio can be used to assess and train current employees using scenarios such as business proposals, work reporting and client response. Kim Min-hwan, head of HRX promotion at SK AX, said that in the AI era corporate competitiveness depends on securing and developing people who can use AI to produce real business results.

He said the tool would help companies secure and develop practically skilled talent with AI capabilities. The articles do not say how the tool's assessments have been validated against actual job performance, nor whether any company other than SK AX has adopted it. They also do not describe any pricing or availability timeline. The announcement appears as one of several AI-related items on the Seoul Economic Daily site that day.

Articles.Title: SK AX Launches AI Tool That Screened 1,800 Applicants in Six Hours - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Cybersecurity Firms Emerge as Core AI Infrastructure
stories.Summary:
Cybersecurity stocks have become a major investment theme in 2026, according to a commentary published by Seoul Economic Daily on October 28, 2026, written by Park Shin-won and framed as a view from Nam Dong-jun, chief executive of Tekton Investment Advisory. The piece traces the shift to Anthropic's Claude Cowork, an AI agent unveiled in early January that could plan and complete assigned tasks on its own rather than only answering questions or producing text. Investors reacted by selling software stocks, fearing that AI agents could reduce the need for existing software businesses, and the IGV exchange-traded fund fell 25% in the first quarter. Cybersecurity firms also dropped early in the year, with Palo Alto Networks and CrowdStrike down 13% and 17% through late March.

From the second quarter onward, the pattern reversed for security firms, which reached record highs while software companies only partly recovered. Palo Alto and CrowdStrike each gained more than 120%, well ahead of the roughly 15% rise in the S&P 500 over the same period. A key turning point came on April 7, when Anthropic introduced its Claude Mythos model but chose not to release it publicly, citing the risk that its ability to find software vulnerabilities and generate attack code could be misused. Instead, the company launched Project Glasswing, a joint response effort with companies it considered trustworthy.

The article argues this shows that AI is not replacing security software and that more powerful AI creates a greater need for integrated security platforms. The commentary points to the security firms' recent results as evidence, noting that third-quarter revenue and order growth at Palo Alto and CrowdStrike beat market estimates and that both raised full-year guidance. It also cites the World Economic Forum, which reported that the share of companies assessing the security of AI tools rose to 64% this year from 37% last year. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei is quoted in Korean-language reporting as saying last month that the pace of AI capability improvements should be slowed because stronger performance raises the risk of uncontrolled behavior.

The author compares this with semiconductors, data centers and power infrastructure, which currently sit at the center of the AI investment boom. The author concludes that security systems become more essential the more AI is deployed inside companies, and that investors should treat cybersecurity as core infrastructure of the AI ecosystem rather than a short-term theme. The article is an opinion piece, and its stock figures and forecasts reflect the author's reading of market data rather than a forecast of future performance. The commentary does not describe any specific next steps beyond this recommendation to investors.

Articles.Title: Cybersecurity Firms Emerge as Core AI Infrastructure - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Ubase Files Patents on AI Call Center Tech That Grasps Intent
stories.Summary:
Ubase, a Korean company, has filed patent applications for two artificial intelligence technologies aimed at call centers, according to a report published on October 29, 2026. The company announced the filings that day, saying the systems can identify the intent and context behind customer questions so responses come faster and routine call center procedures can be automated. The filings cover a multi-agent customer response technology and a system that builds and updates work procedures from call center data. Ubase is also pursuing a separate patent on technology that sorts customer speech into categories.

The first technology uses several AI agents working together to determine what a customer is asking and how it connects to earlier parts of the conversation. Ubase says this reduces response times to within 0.8 seconds, compared with the two to three seconds typically needed by conventional single large language model systems. The second technology analyzes call records with personal information removed, along with product details and policy documents, to produce the procedures and knowledge base that AI-assisted service requires. A separate technology under application breaks customer speech into product, inquiry intent, sentiment and handling route, and Ubase says it identifies inquiry intent for similar products with accuracy above 97%. Based on that analysis, the AI either answers directly or hands the customer to a human agent along with the earlier conversation, so customers do not have to repeat themselves.

Mok Jin-won, Ubase's chief executive, is quoted as saying the AI customer service market is still in an early growth stage in Korea and abroad. He argued that securing core technologies that solve on-the-ground problems ahead of competitors is important. Mok said the filings turn the call center operating expertise Ubase has built up into its own AI technology. He also said the company will keep investing in research and development and in securing technology rights so that a Korean firm can gain recognition in the global market.

The report places these filings within a market Ubase describes as early in its growth, where patent protection for practical systems is becoming a point of competition. The article does not say when the patents are expected to be granted or whether the technologies are already in commercial use. It also does not describe any customers or deployments. More to follow.

Articles.Title: Ubase Files Patents on AI Call Center Tech That Grasps Intent - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Microsoft Leases, Amazon Builds: Rival AI Bets Face Earnings Test
stories.Summary:
Microsoft and Amazon, two of the largest spenders on AI infrastructure, were set to report July to September results one day apart, with Microsoft and Alphabet reporting on October 28 and Amazon and Intel on October 29. The reports put to the test two different strategies for building data center capacity, with Microsoft leasing and Amazon building its own. Investors were focused on cloud performance and any changes to capital spending guidance, since both companies' cloud units are seen as barometers of enterprise AI adoption. The central question, according to one report, was whether the hundreds of billions spent on AI infrastructure is producing meaningful revenue growth.

The expectations laid out in the articles are specific. Wall Street looked for Microsoft to post fiscal first-quarter revenue of $90.75 billion, up 17%, with adjusted earnings per share rising 14% to $4.72. Alphabet's revenue was forecast at $127.83 billion, up 25%, with adjusted profit rising 3% to $2.97 per share. Amazon was projected to report revenue of $202.20 billion, up 12%, and adjusted profit of $1.98 per share, up 2%, while Intel was expected to show revenue up 21% to $16.47 billion and adjusted profit up 72% to $0.40 per share.

The gap between Microsoft and Amazon comes down to how each pays for capacity, according to Seoul Economic Daily. Microsoft signed more than $130 billion in new lease commitments last quarter but spent only $41 billion in cash, and its net cash flow was expected to top $8 billion. Amazon put $54.2 billion into capital expenditure, leaving its cumulative free cash flow for the year at a deficit of $7.6 billion, with net cash outflows projected for a second straight quarter. Amazon Web Services growth was expected to speed up to 38.2% from 36.8%, even as overall revenue growth slows to 12.3% from 19.6%.

The wider technology picture adds context. Last week the Invesco QQQ Trust slipped 0.8% and the iShares Semiconductor ETF fell 3.1%, while a software-focused ETF gained 6%. Elsewhere in the AI supply chain, Oracle said it will install Google's custom TPU chips in its data centers starting next year, and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure president Mahesh Thiagarajan said Nvidia's chips remain the best available. SK hynix reported record third-quarter revenue of 104 trillion won, and its chief financial officer said supply is expected to fall short of demand through 2030. Reuters has reported that Anthropic is eyeing a mid-November public debut at a valuation of up to $1.5 trillion, and the results from Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Intel will show how investors judge the returns on all this spending.

Articles.Title: Microsoft Guards Cash Flow While Amazon's AI Spending Deepens Cash Deficit - Seoul Economic Daily

stories.Headline: Obigo Targets Power Infrastructure Market With Industrial AI Solution BOLT
stories.Summary:
Obigo, a Korean automotive software company, is applying its new industrial physical artificial intelligence solution, BOLT, to power infrastructure for the first time. According to industry sources on October 28, Obigo has been running a proof of concept with a global energy and power infrastructure company since March. An Obigo official said the first test confirmed BOLT's potential for deployment in industrial settings. A second proof of concept with the same company is now underway, adding further AI capabilities.

BOLT connects different types of industrial equipment and communication protocols so that data can be integrated and used by AI agents. The solution currently supports only on-premises deployment, meaning it is installed directly within customers' own environments. Power infrastructure is difficult to upgrade because many facilities run aging equipment that uses different communication protocols and data formats. Obigo says it drew on the equipment integration skills it built in automotive software projects to address this problem. BOLT's AI agents and applications also run in edge computing environments.

Obigo was founded in March 2003 and develops automotive software platforms, including browsers and middleware for in-vehicle infotainment systems. Its major customers are automakers and Tier 1 automotive suppliers, and last year it supplied Hyundai Motor Group with infotainment solutions for global markets. The company is also serving as the lead automotive participant in a Korea Internet & Security Agency project to build a supply chain security model. That project aims to manage software components and vulnerabilities in settings where source code cannot be shared externally. Obigo plans to start with power and energy infrastructure, then expand into defense, rail and shipbuilding, where security and operational stability are critical.

The company's financial results show rapid growth alongside rising costs. Consolidated revenue last year reached 33.5 billion won, up 132.5% from 14.4 billion won in 2024. Its operating loss widened to 3.7 billion won from 2.7 billion won a year earlier. The article links this to a 118.1% rise in selling, general and administrative expenses, which climbed to 37.3 billion won from 17.1 billion won over the same period.

Articles.Title: Obigo Targets Power Infrastructure Market With Industrial AI Solution BOLT - THE ELEC, Korea Electronics Industry Media

stories.Headline: KB Securities Joins SK Telecom's 'AI for Everyone' Initiative to Develop Financial AI Services
stories.Summary:
KB Securities has agreed to join SK Telecom's "AI for Everyone" consortium, a government-backed effort to make artificial intelligence easy for the general public to use. The two companies signed a memorandum of understanding on Oct. 22, and KB Securities announced the deal on Oct. 28. The partnership will explore combining financial AI technology with SK Telecom's AI platform to offer personalized wealth management services. The consortium led by SK Telecom is building an AI assistant that lets users get everyday information and reach various services through conversation.

Under the agreement, KB Securities will discuss taking charge of designing, improving and checking the quality of financial AI functions. SK Telecom will concentrate its part of the work on integrating the AI platform and widening user access. The companies have said they will put financial consumer protection first. Their aim is to present complex financial information in plain terms and help users evaluate their financial assets. They also plan to look at ways to make financial information easier to reach for older adults and people with limited financial knowledge.

KB Securities has already applied generative AI to analyze financial products and investment information and to review how financial products are sold. It runs its own financial AI agent service, called Kkaebi AI. Through the partnership, the company plans to bring those capabilities into SK Telecom's platform. Park Jae-man, head of the AI and Digital Division at KB Securities, said the design and quality checks of the financial AI functions would give customers accurate, easy-to-understand information. He added that this would help them make informed decisions.

Articles.Title: KB Securities Joins SK Telecom's 'AI for Everyone' Initiative to Develop Financial AI Services - THE ELEC, Korea Electronics Industry Media

stories.Headline: WISE iTech Launches YouTube AI Analytics Service
stories.Summary:
WISE iTech, an artificial intelligence and data specialist, has entered the YouTube content analytics market with a new service called Tumeet. Company CEO Kim Da-san announced the launch at a press conference held at voco Seoul Myeongdong in central Seoul on Oct. 27. The firm, which has mainly served businesses and public institutions, plans to start with a subscription model and later connect advertisers with creators. The company says it is building on the large volume of data already generated on YouTube.

Tumeet analyzes daily YouTube content and channel data, offering 100 trending keywords across 13 categories. Users can track shifts in interest for each keyword and view related videos and search terms. When a creator links a YouTube channel, the service reviews views, subscriber counts and watch time, along with viewer sources, search terms and geographic distribution. It also lets users compare their channel with similar ones. The company additionally introduced Tumeet PD, which suggests titles, descriptions and tags and flags recurring viewer requests in comments.

WISE iTech said its researchers and partners demonstrated how the tool has been used in practice. The company signed a memorandum of understanding with Quan Entertainment in July and deployed Tumeet on Haha PD, a channel with 1.17 million subscribers. Producer Park Shin-woo said the team now makes decisions based on data rather than intuition. He cited the "Expedition" series, whose engagement rose over time after initially attracting little attention, a change the team spotted through the tool's notifications. The company described this as a clear example of the service's value.

The company aims to secure 500 paying customers and 1,000 total users, including free users, by early 2027. Over the longer term, it plans a product placement matching business that would analyze each channel's audience and content performance to help advertisers choose creators, but the articles say this remains at the conceptual stage. The initial focus is South Korea's YouTube market, with improved analytics for Korean-language content. The company is also considering expansion to TikTok and Instagram. CEO Kim said the goal is to let anyone use data as a basis for content and channel decisions.

Articles.Title: WISE iTech Launches YouTube AI Analytics Service - THE ELEC, Korea Electronics Industry Media

stories.Headline: LG Uplus Wins Global Recognition for AI Optimization
stories.Summary:
LG Uplus said on October 29 that two of its papers on AI token optimization were accepted at the on-device intelligence workshop of NeurIPS 2026, one of the world's top three AI conferences. The conference is set to take place in Sydney, Australia, starting December 6. The company framed the recognition as evidence that its AI work can run efficiently on smartphones, where memory and power are limited. The research centers on how fast and efficiently AI processes tokens, the units it uses to read questions and produce answers.

LG Uplus built a small language model for call services and applied lightweighting and inference acceleration to suit smartphone hardware. According to the company, processing speed rose about 4.5 times over the existing method while the model kept the performance level of the latest cloud AI. Power efficiency improved as well, with battery consumption reduced by about 77 percent. A second strand of the work concerns on-device learning, which trains AI inside the phone so that personal data does not have to be sent to an external server. The company reported that this streamlined approach reached accuracy equal to models trained on a server.

LG Uplus CTO Lee Sang-yeop described the paper acceptance as recognition of the company's work on running and training AI efficiently in constrained environments. He said the technologies will be applied to real services and that the research scope will later expand to server environments. The company is reviewing plans to bring these optimization capabilities into its services, with the aim of offering customers a faster and more convenient AI experience. The announcement comes as the AI industry's competition increasingly focuses on data processing efficiency rather than model performance alone.

Articles.Title: LG Uplus Wins Global Recognition for AI Optimization - Businesskorea

stories.Headline: Most tweens and teens use AI for schoolwork and emotional support, a new survey shows
stories.Summary:
A new survey of more than 5,000 American tweens and teens, conducted by the Jed Foundation, found that most of them use AI chatbots for schoolwork and for emotional support. Fifty-eight percent said they use chatbots for help with schoolwork, and a similar share turn to them when they feel sad, stressed, lonely or overwhelmed. The report was covered by NPR in a segment reported by Rhitu Chatterjee and published on October 28, 2026. Students interviewed for the story described using chatbots to practice sample test questions and to ease worries about exams. One 15-year-old in Texas said he has asked a chatbot whether he would be fine after a difficult chemistry test.

The survey data also linked chatbot use for companionship or during distress with worse mental health overall. Kayla Anderson, vice president of research and evaluation at the Jed Foundation, said those who used chatbots this way reported higher loneliness, less resilience, and a history of suicidal ideation and attempts. She stressed that the data cannot show whether AI use causes these problems or whether students already in distress are more likely to turn to AI. The article does not describe any new rule, law or requirement that the survey itself imposes. It reports only the findings and the researchers' interpretation of them.

Anne Maheux, a developmental psychologist at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, said preliminary research suggests the relationship likely runs in both directions. She described findings from her team's work showing that middle schoolers who use chatbots for companionship become lonelier over time, with similar results among young adults. Her explanation is that AI handles momentary problems in ways that help in the moment but may weaken people's ability to handle everyday stress over time. The article does not give a timeline for further research or any planned policy response from the researchers or other officials.

Articles.Title: Most tweens and teens use AI for schoolwork and emotional support, a new survey shows

stories.Headline: Mark Zuckerberg admits the AI restructuring isn't going all that great, report says
stories.Summary:
Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg has acknowledged that the company's AI restructuring is not going as well as hoped, according to a report published on October 28, 2026. The admission came during an internal town hall held on a Thursday, which Reuters examined. Earlier in the year, Meta laid off 8,000 people in May, citing an AI push, and moved another 7,000 employees into AI-focused roles. At the time, Zuckerberg had described AI in an internal memo as the most consequential technology of our lifetimes.

During the town hall, Zuckerberg reportedly said that AI agents had not progressed as quickly as he had expected. He also said the restructuring had not been as clean as it could have been and that Meta executives had miscalculated the timing of the changes. According to the report, some of the company's top people had worried earlier this year that Meta was not adapting fast enough to an AI-driven world. The restructuring has also drawn a company-wide backlash over AI-related employee tracking and reports of low employee morale. Meta responded to the morale concerns with measures that included snacks.

Zuckerberg is said to expect more significant benefits from the company's AI investments within the next three to six months. The article does not describe any change in direction beyond that expectation. It also notes that Meta is facing other pressures, including a growing privacy backlash against its smart glasses. Those glasses are now reportedly subject to a subscription for unlimited access to all features.

Articles.Title: Mark Zuckerberg admits the AI restructuring isn't going all that great, report says

stories.Headline: How this private school in Palo Alto uses AI to support students
stories.Summary:
Alpha School, a private school in Palo Alto, uses artificial intelligence to shape each student's daily learning, and the school is one of 40 Alpha Schools across the country. The approach is reported by NBC Bay Area, which describes AI being part of the school's routine every morning, even for young children. The school says the technology works in the background rather than through chatbots, guiding each student along an individual learning path. Lesson plans are tailored by AI so that instruction is as efficient as possible, in contrast to a conventional classroom with one teacher and many students.

Students at the school spend two hours a day on math and science before turning to other skills. Alpha School co-founder Mackenzie Price said that finishing academics in the morning frees the rest of the day for building the skills she described as true human flourishing. Dean of parents Emma Ludwick said the school treats AI as a tool to optimize, support and individualize learning in service of the child. The school is also said to be working with public schools to share ideas. Staff say the aim is to serve each student rather than replace the human role in education.

The articles are candid about the cost and reach of the model. Tuition is $75,000 a year, and the school acknowledges that its use of AI and its division of the day into learning blocks is not suited to every family. Its leaders say the school offers financial aid. The report also notes that the path students take at the school may not lead them to a technology company, though the report does not say how often that happens. The piece is a feature rather than a news report of a specific event, and it does not describe any regulatory action or next steps for the school.

Articles.Title: How this private school in Palo Alto uses AI to support students

stories.Headline: Could AI give Colorado more warning before damaging hailstorms?
stories.Summary:
Researchers at Colorado State University are working to improve hail forecasts in Colorado using artificial intelligence, aiming to give people more time to protect property and reach safety. Damaging hail can form quickly inside severe thunderstorms, which often leaves homeowners, farmers and businesses with little time to prepare. The report, published by CBS News Colorado on October 28, 2026, describes the effort as a response to that narrow window. The team wants forecasts that can point more precisely to where hail is likely to fall. The research combines two AI models built for different timescales.

One model, called Hail Storm Scope, uses radar data to forecast conditions up to two hours ahead. The other, the CSU Machine Learning Probabilities model, estimates the likelihood of severe storms and hail as far as eight days out. Researchers are working to connect the two and refine them with high-resolution weather data to make forecasts more specific to Colorado and the surrounding region. Kristen Rasmussen, an associate professor at CSU, said hail accounts for 25 to 55 percent of homeowners insurance claims on a state basis, which is why the project focuses on it.

The team also plans field experiments in the spring, using radar and other instruments to check whether the models predict where hail reaches the ground. Better advance warning could help people act before a storm arrives. Farmers could learn more about threats to their crops, and businesses could have time to protect vehicles and solar panels. Event organizers could use improved forecasts to move people to shelter before severe weather reaches outdoor venues.

The team is also studying how hail risk may change as the climate warms. Rasmussen said hail season in Colorado currently runs from late March through late August or early September, but climate analysis suggests it may shift earlier in spring and later into fall. Her team's analysis also indicates severe weather could increase in parts of the region, especially in densely populated areas such as the Denver metro area. Rasmussen stressed that human meteorologists remain essential even as AI tools improve.

She said forecasters' experience in particular regions helps them judge which models to trust, and that AI adds another layer of information rather than replacing their judgment. She also noted that the quality of the data used to train the models strongly affects their performance, so the team is working to measure how well predictions match actual hail observations. The findings could also inform long-term decisions about building codes and materials, including stronger roofing designed to withstand hail. The team hopes to deploy improved forecasting tools later next year, with the goal of giving forecasters more detailed, locally relevant hail-risk information.

Articles.Title: Could AI give Colorado more warning before damaging hailstorms?

stories.Headline: Jim Cramer says Microsoft is winning the AI spending battle — and Alphabet is paying the price
stories.Summary:
On Thursday, October 29, 2026, CNBC's Jim Cramer said that Wall Street's reaction to the latest earnings from Microsoft and Alphabet shows that investors have shifted from rewarding heavy artificial intelligence spending to favoring financial discipline and returns. Earlier this year, Microsoft's restrained spending had raised worries that it could fall behind rivals, while Alphabet was rewarded for pouring money into data centers and custom chips. Cramer's comments followed Microsoft and Alphabet reports released Wednesday night, which he said changed that picture. Cramer's Charitable Trust, the portfolio run by CNBC's Investing Club, owns shares of both companies.

Microsoft beat earnings and revenue expectations, and revenue for its Azure cloud business grew 48% from a year earlier. Its capital expenditures and finance leases totaled $45.2 billion, below Wall Street's forecasts. Cramer praised the company for pairing strong cloud growth with positive free cash flow, and he said its AI assistant for businesses, Copilot, had started slowly but was becoming a strong success. Alphabet, by contrast, missed earnings and revenue expectations, with Search and YouTube ad revenue both coming in below estimates. Although Google Cloud revenue more than doubled, its shares fell sharply in Thursday's session, which Cramer described as the stock's worst day ever.

Cramer credited Microsoft's results to CEO Satya Nadella and CFO Amy Hood, whom he called a shrewd CEO and a tight-fisted, canny finance chief who run the company like a business rather than a science project. He said Microsoft's stock is now set to soar and that it is a buy at its current level. He was far more skeptical of Alphabet, arguing that its AI investments are harder to justify as cash generation weakens. The company expects capital expenditures of $195 billion to $205 billion this year, and its free cash flow turned negative for a second straight quarter. Cramer also flagged $27.6 billion in remaining authorized stock sales as a possible drag on shares, and he said he would not buy more Alphabet while waiting for analysts to revise their estimates.

Articles.Title: Jim Cramer says Microsoft is winning the AI spending battle — and Alphabet is paying the price

stories.Headline: PACOM Looks to AI Agents for Faster Intelligence, Targeting
stories.Summary:
Indo-Pacific Command, known as PACOM, is moving to bring AI agents into its intelligence and targeting work, according to officials who spoke at TechNet Indo-Pacific. The plans were laid out in remarks reported by GovCIO Media & Research on October 28, 2026. Military leaders said adversaries are advancing their own capabilities, which has pushed defense officials to use AI and synthetic intelligence to speed analysis, targeting and decisions. Rear Adm. Jeffrey Buschmann, the command's J2 intelligence director, said AI had moved from a buzzword to a tool that is now built into nearly every process at PACOM.

The command is prioritizing interoperable tools, common data standards and AI-powered capabilities to keep pace with adversaries. Brig. Chris Alder, the Australian Army vice director for intelligence at PACOM, said a common data framework and shared data ontologies would let nations share information. He said that when such a standard is in place, targeting latency falls from minutes to seconds. The command is also exploring agentic AI to automate parts of the targeting cycle, and Alder said officials want a human kept firmly on the loop for critical decisions.

Chief SI officer Scott Brunstetter, whose position was created about 15 months ago, said PACOM is studying SI for warning, targeting, predictive analysis and rapid software prototyping. One priority is a common operating picture intelligence data layer that would pull intelligence from several sources and improve situational awareness across the command. Brunstetter said agentic AI is the next critical step and that the command must reimagine how it works as change accelerates. He also said the command does not blindly trust these tools, and that it wants evidence that helps analysts understand how the technology works.

Scott Buchanan, chief of the Intelligence Information Systems Division at PACOM, argued that clinging to existing systems would be a recipe for failure. He stressed deploying tools that can run without depending on data centers in Hawaii or the continental United States. Brunstetter said smaller, mission-specific AI models could need less computing power and energy while still supporting operations at the tactical edge. Buschmann also pointed to the Navy's long experience with nuclear power as a possible advantage for future operations. The articles do not give dates for when these capabilities will be fielded, so the plans remain at the stage of intent and exploration.

Articles.Title: PACOM Looks to AI Agents for Faster Intelligence, Targeting

stories.Headline: Cognitive Surrender vs. AI Literacy: Higher-Ed Experts Debate AI
stories.Summary:
In a debate at Johns Hopkins University on Tuesday, higher education leaders agreed that artificial intelligence has caused problems for learning so far but disagreed about how large those problems are. The debate was held at the university's Homewood campus as part of the Hopkins Forum series. It asked whether generative AI will enhance or stunt postsecondary learning. Opponents said the technology weakens critical thinking and lets students hand in work they do not understand, while others said the effects depend on how educators and students use it. The debaters agreed that AI is already changing higher education and forcing a rethink of how students are taught and assessed.

Gary Marcus, a psychology professor at New York University, argued that students often use chatbots in place of their own thinking, a pattern he called cognitive surrender. Cathy O'Neil, a mathematician and algorithmic auditor, described a colleague who had students read their essays aloud, and some could not pronounce words in them or explain what they meant. She said AI can weaken the systems schools use to check whether students are keeping up, since a student could earn high grades with little real understanding. O'Neil also warned that students without human guidance may be more vulnerable to this kind of surrender. Ravi Pendse, chief information officer at the University of Michigan, argued that students are not always inclined to take shortcuts when they have the chance.

He said AI is not inherently harmful but places new responsibility on institutions to guide students in using it well. Pendse said that the answer to false information from AI tools is AI literacy, not avoiding the tools altogether. Edward Maloney, an English professor and executive director of Georgetown University's Center for New Designs in Learning and Scholarship, said AI exposes weak points in higher education, including large lectures and standard exams. He argued that AI could make those methods more transactional but could also allow more individualized instruction, with tools acting as tutors or debate partners. The panelists were divided on the remedy.

O'Neil said that AI should not be used to fix problems that AI has exposed, and she favored a return to oral and in-person exams. Pendse said those same assessment methods could work alongside assignments that build AI literacy. A survey of in-person attendees before and after the debate showed movement toward the "enhance" side, which grew from 26 percent to just under 40 percent. The "stunt" side, which started at 38 percent, ended at just over 40 percent, so opinion remains split. Marcus summed up the common ground by saying that educators need to think differently about pedagogy now.

Articles.Title: Cognitive Surrender vs. AI Literacy: Higher-Ed Experts Debate AI

stories.Headline: Generative AI and News Report 2026: From standalone tools to information infrastructure
stories.Summary:
Researchers at the Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism published a report on 29 October 2026, titled "Generative AI and News Report 2026," which examines how people use generative AI systems and what they think of its use in news. The survey covered nine countries: Argentina, Australia, Denmark, Finland, France, Japan, Norway, the United Kingdom, and the United States. It is a follow-up to earlier reports based on 2024 and 2025 data collected in six of those countries. The authors are Felix Simon, Rasmus Kleis Nielsen, and Richard Fletcher, and the report's data was released in late October.

The findings show that use of standalone AI chatbots is growing quickly, with weekly use rising from 34% last year to 51% in 2026 across the six countries with past data. Daily use nearly doubled over the same period, from 7% in 2024 to 16% in 2025 and 28% in 2026. ChatGPT remains the market leader, with weekly use rising from 22% to 34%, while Gemini grew from 11% to 24%, Copilot from 6% to 11%, and Claude from 1% to 7%. Using AI to get information has become the most common use, reaching 38% in 2026, and 9% of respondents now use AI for news, up from 3% in 2024.

Only 12% of respondents say they are comfortable with news made entirely by AI. The report describes these patterns as findings from the survey itself, and it does not assign responsibility for any of them to a particular actor. The authors note that trust in the major systems has grown as people become more familiar with them, though many people still neither trust nor distrust them. They also say that most people who rely on AI for information find the answers trustworthy, with 72% of those who used it for news saying they trust the output, but that convenience matters more to users than reliability.

Respondents were more pessimistic about the news media's use of AI than about scientists or healthcare professionals, and the authors say that pessimism tends to stem from perceived dishonesty about AI use rather than doubts about competence. The report's context is that AI is becoming part of the infrastructure through which people find information, appearing in search summaries, on social platforms, and in news products themselves. The authors frame the 2026 survey as a continuation of their earlier work, and the articles do not say what further studies or steps will follow. More to follow.

Articles.Title: Generative AI and News Report 2026: From standalone tools to information infrastructure

stories.Headline: Microsoft launches new MAI family of AI models for reasoning, voice, coding, and images
stories.Summary:
Microsoft used its Build 2026 developer conference on Tuesday to announce a new family of in-house AI models, along with several other products. The announcements were made during CEO Satya Nadella's keynote and span the company's product stack, from silicon and operating systems to cloud infrastructure. The centerpiece is MAI-Thinking-1, the company's first reasoning model, which is described as mid-sized with 35 billion active parameters and a 128K context window. Microsoft says it was built for efficiency and low token cost.

Six more models were announced alongside it, covering image generation, transcription, voice, and code. They are MAI-Image-2.5 with a Flash variant, MAI-Transcribe-1.5, MAI-Voice-2 with a Flash variant, and MAI-Code-1. MAI-Transcribe-1.5 will be available soon in 43 languages, while MAI-Voice-2 and its Flash variant are already available in 15 additional languages with multiple voice options. Microsoft plans to make all of the models available in Foundry and a new dedicated environment called MAI Playground.

Kyle Daigle, Microsoft's Developer CMO and COO of GitHub, said at a virtual media briefing that MAI-Thinking-1 was designed for complex multi-step instructions, long-context reasoning, and code generation. He said the model was built from scratch on commercially licensed data. The company says independent evaluators preferred it over Anthropic's Claude Sonnet 4.6, and that it matches Claude Opus 4.6 on the SWE Bench Pro coding benchmark. Access differs by model, with MAI-Thinking-1 in private preview in Foundry, MAI-Image-2.5 already live in PowerPoint and OneDrive, and MAI-Code-1 available now in Copilot and VS Code.

Microsoft also announced Microsoft Scout, a personal agent that handles scheduling, meeting prep, and routine tasks through Teams and Outlook, and it begins rolling out to Frontier customers today. On hardware, the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box, powered by NVIDIA's RTX Spark chip, offers up to one petaflop of AI compute and 128 gigabytes of unified memory, with the ability to run models up to 120 billion parameters locally. It ships later this year in the US. Microsoft Discovery is now generally available, and Windows is being repositioned as an agent-native runtime through a sandboxing system called Microsoft Execution Containers, which is in preview.

Articles.Title: Microsoft launches new MAI family of AI models for reasoning, voice, coding, and images

stories.Headline: Microsoft Sees Enterprise AI Adoption Accelerate as Copilot Usage Grows
stories.Summary:
Microsoft reported its fiscal first-quarter earnings on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, and said enterprises are moving AI from experiments into systems that run business processes. CEO Satya Nadella pointed to Unilever, Rolls-Royce and Austrian lender Raiffeisen Bank International as examples. Revenue for the quarter reached $92.3 billion, up 19%, and the company beat expectations on revenue, operating income and earnings per share. Microsoft Cloud revenue rose 30% to $63.9 billion, and Azure revenue grew 48%. Nadella said customers now care whether AI delivers reliable results, controls costs and operates securely.

Unilever is automating order intake and trade promotion disputes. Rolls-Royce is using AI to manage maintenance planning, inventory and supply chains for jet engines with about 30,000 parts. Raiffeisen has deployed AI across more than 20 business processes, including credit-related workflows. Microsoft also reported that daily Copilot users rose nearly 50% from the prior quarter and more than five times from a year ago. Customers with more than 50,000 Copilot seats grew more than eightfold from a year earlier.

Microsoft is also changing how it charges for AI. Alongside per-user subscriptions, it now offers consumption-based billing for agents that handle more complex tasks, and the number of Copilot customers using that billing grew more than 75% in the quarter. Nadella said IT departments typically fund subscriptions for everyday AI, while individual business units can pay for higher-value agent work. CFO Amy Hood said consumption pricing outside software development will likely move more slowly, because it requires changes in sales practices and customer education. Volkswagen recently announced plans to deploy Copilot to more than 330,000 employees.

Other results from the call included more than 50 million agents listed in Agent 365's registry, up more than 30% from the prior quarter, and more than 7.6 billion agent activities audited through Microsoft Purview. Agents now open more than a third of all pull requests on GitHub. On the consumer side, Microsoft 365 consumer cloud revenue rose 17%, with growth slowing as the company lapped an earlier price increase. Nadella said he expects the shift from experimentation to operational AI to continue.

Articles.Title: Microsoft Sees Enterprise AI Adoption Accelerate as Copilot Usage Grows

stories.Headline: Nvidia Finds Itself at the Center of an AI Spy Saga
stories.Summary:
On October 29, 2026, The New York Times published an investigation reporting that Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang may have been the target of Chinese espionage. According to the report, US authorities identified Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen and executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data center company, as a possible operative for the Chinese government, with whom Jensen Huang had developed a close relationship. Alice Huang shares no family connection with the Nvidia chief. Megaspeed buys Nvidia chips to run data centers that sell computing power to Chinese AI labs, including Alibaba's Qwen team.

US intelligence agencies had been conducting electronic surveillance of Alice Huang over allegations that she helped sell advanced Nvidia chips to China in violation of US law. During that surveillance, officials reportedly found she was also allegedly passing information to the Chinese government in Beijing. The articles do not say what information was shared or how valuable it might be, but the Times reports that the investigation and surveillance are ongoing. Jensen Huang was not warned by the US government, reportedly because doing so could have jeopardized the probe, according to people with knowledge of the matter cited by the Times.

Nvidia responded through a spokesperson, who said Jensen Huang's interactions with Alice Huang were "not unusual or unexpected" because he meets with thousands of customer executives each year. The company said customers such as Megaspeed are no different from many other regional cloud customers and do not receive sensitive trade secrets. Nvidia also said it trusts that the US government would alert it if it considered any person a threat to American industry. The Times also reports that Trump was briefed on the investigation into Alice Huang a year ago and chose not to act. The White House, the Justice Department and Megaspeed did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

The story comes against a backdrop of intense competition over advanced AI chips, which have made Nvidia the world's most valuable company, with a market capitalization of $5 trillion this year. The Biden administration banned Chinese sales of a series of advanced Nvidia chips in 2022, but President Donald Trump relaxed those rules in 2025, and the US government now receives 15% of revenue from Nvidia and AMD on certain chip sales to China. Reports also show that illegal efforts to smuggle banned chips to China continue. The article notes that Trump has a friendly relationship with many Big Tech leaders, including Jensen Huang, and that this has resulted in millions in personal donations to the president. It also notes a separate FBI arrest this month of a Saudi Arabian national accused of planting a recording device in an OpenAI executive conference room.

Articles.Title: Nvidia Finds Itself at the Center of an AI Spy Saga

stories.Headline: Fake Anthropic AI previews lure in overeager employees
stories.Summary:
A phishing campaign is luring employees with fake invitations to a private Anthropic AI preview, according to new research from the cybersecurity company Cofense, published on October 29, 2026. The attackers send what appears to be a GoTo Webinar invitation, and when recipients click the link to register, they are sent to a compromised page built to steal their Google or Microsoft login credentials. Security tools often do not block GoTo Webinar meeting emails, which helps the messages reach inboxes. The sender name is shown as "Austin from nthropic," with the first letter of the company name missing, a small inconsistency the researchers flagged as a warning sign.

The lure works by appealing to exclusivity and fear of missing out, and the email describes a select, invitation-only session on AI systems and frontier models. The link is routed through a URL shortener and a link generated by Zapier, a legitimate company, which helps it evade email filters. Recipients must pass a Cloudflare CAPTCHA page, then reach a page that imitates a Zoom invitation and asks for a work email address. A second CAPTCHA appears before the fake Google or Microsoft login page, and the researchers said these checks can also block security scanners from analyzing the attack. The Google page reportedly captured only usernames, which the researchers suspect is a misconfiguration, while the Microsoft page collected both usernames and passwords.

The researchers advised staff to check whether branding stays consistent from the email to the login page and to look for small misspellings. They also stressed that the URL and domain, not the logo or design, determine whether a login page is legitimate. Frank Dickson of Dickson Research said enterprises should verify any AI preview invitation through an account team or a known contact, treat changing branding as a red flag, and roll out phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication such as passkeys. He also argued that employees should not be the last line of defense, and that anyone who entered credentials should reset them and review account activity. Dickson further noted that attackers tend to target whatever technology is currently in the news, so similar lures using other names are likely to follow.

Articles.Title: Fake Anthropic AI previews lure in overeager employees

stories.Headline: SAG-AFTRA, WGA & AFM Warn Of "Harms" Of Unlicensed AI Training
stories.Summary:
The unions SAG-AFTRA, the Writers Guild of America East and West, and the American Federation of Musicians filed a joint amicus brief on Thursday, October 29, 2026, in a New York federal court. The filing is part of an ongoing copyright infringement case in which OpenAI faces news outlets and writers over the use of their content to train AI language models. The unions asked the judge to reject a categorical fair use exemption for AI training and to treat each case on its own terms. They say the company is taking the work of middle- and working-class people to build its technology without permission or payment.

The brief runs 34 pages and argues that a blanket exemption would allow a potentially enormous transfer of value from creators to corporations. It stresses the human element in writing, with particular attention to news, which is central to the case. The unions contend that the harms of unlicensed training reach beyond large news organizations to the many professionals who do the work. They conclude that the dispute is an ordinary copyright matter that should be decided case by case, not through a sweeping rule.

The consolidated case pits OpenAI against the New York Times, several Florida and Arkansas newspapers, The Intercept, and a group of prominent authors. Those authors include Ta-Nehisi Coates, George R.R. Martin, John Grisham, Michael Connelly, Jonathan Franzen, and Jodi Picoult, along with Sarah Silverman and the Authors Guild. Several other writers, among them David Baldacci, George Saunders, and Scott Turow, are also part of the litigation. The unions' AI positions have deep roots, since the issue was central to the 2023 strikes and resurfaced in 2026 bargaining.

The brief links the court fight to those negotiations. The writers and actors guilds secured a notice-and-bargaining right for third-party licenses of covered work used to train commercial generative AI systems. The unions argue that a ruling calling AI training categorically fair use would make those agreed terms meaningless and would harm copyright owners and the people who create the work. The case's outcome could therefore shape both the courts' approach to AI training and the labor protections negotiated in Hollywood. The articles do not say when the judge is expected to rule.

Articles.Title: SAG-AFTRA, WGA & AFM Warn Of "Harms" Of Unlicensed AI Training

stories.Headline: Raoul Pal Says AI Spending Has No Ceiling. Are Tech Stocks in Danger?
stories.Summary:
Raoul Pal, the Real Vision CEO, has argued that the world's largest technology companies can keep spending on artificial intelligence almost indefinitely. The argument comes as recent earnings show how costly that spending is becoming. Alphabet's shares fell after its Wednesday report, when AI investments pushed quarterly free cash flow to negative $9.07 billion. Microsoft's shares rose after it reported $18.6 billion in positive free cash flow, which highlights the gap between the two companies.

Pal's case rests on a self-reinforcing loop in which companies use the AI they build, become more productive, generate more cash and reinvest it in more infrastructure. He puts their debt at roughly 3.5% of their stock-market value and compares the expansion to the railroad boom, which lasted 35 years. Amazon expects to spend about $220 billion in 2026, while Alphabet has budgeted up to $205 billion, figures that include infrastructure beyond AI. Microsoft's Azure cloud revenue grew 48%, while Alphabet's cloud revenue more than doubled but its spending outpaced its cash generation.

Pal's optimism faces a challenge from credit markets. Union Bancaire Privée estimates that five major hyperscalers will spend $820 billion in 2026, above their projected $750 billion in operating cash flow. The Bank of England has warned that AI infrastructure increasingly relies on borrowing and complex financing arrangements. Former BitMEX CEO Arthur Hayes has warned of an AI overbuild followed by a crash and potential bailout, a risk that could reach Bitcoin miners such as MARA and CleanSpark, which are expanding into AI infrastructure. Amazon's October 29 earnings are the next test of whether strong cloud demand and improving cash flow can support the spending.

Articles.Title: Raoul Pal Says AI Spending Has No Ceiling. Are Tech Stocks in Danger?

stories.Headline: Microsoft Copilot for finance: Purpose-built for the way finance teams work
stories.Summary:
Microsoft has expanded Copilot for finance professionals, announcing more than 25 new finance skills and partner-built plugins across Microsoft Copilot on October 29, 2026. The company introduced finance skills in Copilot in Excel back in June 2026, and this latest release extends them to accounting, capital markets, and broader finance work. Excel is now embedded directly in the Copilot app, so users can analyze, edit, and co-author workbooks from within Chat or Cowork. Microsoft says Work IQ grounds Copilot in organizational knowledge such as the close calendar and deal-team conversations, so it can work from more than the file in front of the user.

The new accounting capabilities, available in Frontier for Copilot in Excel and Cowork, aim to reduce repetitive manual work in three main areas. Copilot can compare balances and transactions to identify discrepancies and prepare reconciling items for review, and it can draft accruals, reclassifications, allocations, reversals, and recurring entries with checks for required inputs and balanced entries. It can also analyze performance against plan and prepare reporting that explains what changed. In a seven-day limited Insiders period, more than 8,000 unique users invoked accounting skills more than 44,000 times across more than 18,000 Copilot conversations. Finance professionals can also choose to start an audit trail that records what Copilot changed and why in their chat history.

Microsoft says Copilot is designed to support professional review rather than replace it, and that finance professionals retain control over recommendations, decisions, approvals, and actions. In Excel, Copilot can summarize recent activity, identify when and by whom specific changes were made, and selectively reverse individual edits without disrupting the rest of the workbook. The company states that Copilot processes prompts and responses within the Microsoft 365 service boundary with enterprise data protection, honors existing permissions and sensitivity labels, and does not use prompts, responses, or documents to train the underlying foundation models. Brian Jones, corporate vice president of the Excel Product Group, leads the work described in the post.

Availability varies by feature. Finance skills in Copilot in Excel and the Capital Markets and Finance plugins in Cowork are generally available, while the accounting capabilities are in Frontier, and the Dynamics 365 ERP apps plugin and partner plugins are beginning to roll out through the Microsoft plugin registry. Fabric IQ is generally available in Cowork. Third-party services may require separate licensing, subscriptions, authentication, or administrator enablement from the providers. Microsoft lists partners including Intuit QuickBooks, Xero, FactSet, Morningstar, S&P Global, and LSEG, among others, and cites early feedback from firms such as EY Ireland and Zurich Insurance North America.

Articles.Title: Microsoft Copilot for finance: Purpose-built for the way finance teams work

stories.Headline: Microsoft's Leadership in AI Remains 'Underappreciated,' Morgan Stanley Says
stories.Summary:
Morgan Stanley said on Thursday, October 29, 2026, that Microsoft's leadership in artificial intelligence remains underappreciated. The bank's analysts pointed to third-quarter results that showed accelerating growth and visible returns on the company's AI spending. The company reported adjusted earnings late Wednesday of $4.89 per diluted share on revenue of $92.28 billion. Analysts surveyed by FactSet had expected $4.71 per share on $90.62 billion in revenue.

The Microsoft Cloud segment drove much of the strength, with Azure growing 48 percent in constant currency from a year earlier despite delays in third-party capacity. Morgan Stanley said Microsoft 365 Commercial Cloud grew 18 percent, supported by seat volume and higher average revenue per user. The analysts described an "Enterprise AI Flywheel," in which Microsoft's positions in infrastructure, models, data and applications create demand across the whole stack. They said the platform connects models with enterprise data, orchestrates workloads and monetizes the activity that results. According to the note, these investments can support revenue growth in the high teens and earnings growth above 20 percent.

Morgan Stanley reiterated its overweight rating on the stock and raised its price target to $650 from $600. The firm's view is that Microsoft benefits as enterprise adoption and consumption of AI grow. The article's related-story links show that other brokerages, including BofA, have also written about Microsoft's AI positioning and monetization in recent months. The sidebar links do not state any additional findings about the company's future results. The report itself is a broker's analysis rather than a company statement, and the article does not describe any response from Microsoft.

Articles.Title: Microsoft's Leadership in AI Remains 'Underappreciated,' Morgan Stanley Says

stories.Headline: Can an AI chatbot help women recognize heart disease?
stories.Summary:
A team at the University of California, San Francisco has built HeartBot, an AI chatbot designed to help women learn about heart disease, and the project is described in an article published on October 28, 2026. The tool was led by Yoshimi Fukuoka, a nurse scientist and professor at UCSF's School of Nursing, and it began in 2021 with research from a group that included cardiovascular nursing scientists, linguists, computer scientists and others from UCSF, UCLA and UC Davis. The chatbot answers questions about the basics of heart disease, heart attack symptoms, risk factors and prevention, and it can recall earlier conversations to personalize its replies. Its goal is to raise awareness so that women recognize warning signs and seek medical help when needed.

The current version, HeartBot II, was upgraded in 2025 and moved from a text-message format to a chatbot app built on a large language model. Its answers draw on a core knowledge bank that the researchers wrote to reduce the risk of false or misleading medical information. The team also rewrote certain terms, such as "risk factors," in everyday language after feedback showed the medical wording was not always clear. The app is currently available to trial participants through the Apple App Store and Google Play Store. The researchers plan to release it to the broader public only after its efficacy and safety are established.

The motivation behind the tool is that heart disease remains the leading cause of death among women and affects more than 60 million women in the United States, with the highest rates among non-Hispanic Black women. The article cites the American Heart Association's figure that one in three women dies from heart disease. It also notes that women who knew heart disease was the leading cause of death fell from 65% in 2009 to 44% in 2019, with the steepest declines among Black, Hispanic and younger women. Fukuoka said that traditional media campaigns alone were not enough and that a more innovative approach was needed, especially for underserved groups.

To test whether the bot actually works, Fukuoka is running a six-month randomized controlled trial with 201 female patients of UCSF Health. Half of the participants will get immediate access to the HeartBot II sessions, while the other half will receive access later and serve as a control group. Researchers will compare how well each group retains heart disease information over time. Fukuoka's longer-term vision is to test the tool with several thousand women and eventually make it widely available, possibly through QR codes placed in clinics and on public transportation. The article frames the central question as whether a conversation with AI can help women recognize heart attack warning signs and know what to do when minutes matter.

Articles.Title: Can an AI chatbot help women recognize heart disease?

stories.Headline: Accelerate agentic AI with NVIDIA Nemotron models on Amazon EKS and SageMaker HyperPod EKS
stories.Summary:
Amazon Web Services published a blog post on October 29, 2026, describing how to run NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Super VL model on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS), EKS Auto Mode, and Amazon SageMaker HyperPod EKS. The model is a 120-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts system that activates 12 billion parameters for each token it processes. It handles text, image, document, and video input, and produces text output. The post joins Nemotron 3.5 Super VL to other Nemotron models that AWS already offers, including Nemotron 3 Nano, Nano Omni, Super, Ultra, and Nemotron 3.5 Lightning.

The model's design aims to keep compute costs close to those of a much smaller model while still holding the full set of weights in GPU memory. It uses a hybrid architecture that mixes Mamba-2, attention, and expert layers, with a vision encoder for visual inputs and a context window of up to 1 million tokens. According to the article, NVIDIA reports scores of 63.44 percent on Hermes Bench, 87.05 percent on LangChain agent evaluations, and 80.8 percent on the CharXiv chart-reasoning benchmark. The post lists minimum GPU counts by hardware type: eight B200 or GB200 GPUs for the BF16 version, or two for the NVFP4 version; four B300 or GB300 GPUs for NVFP4 at minimum; eight H200 GPUs for BF16 or four for NVFP4; and sixteen H100 GPUs for BF16 or eight for NVFP4. The deployment pattern runs the same Kubernetes manifests across all three orchestration options, and the authors describe validating the setup on p6-b200.48xlarge and p5en.48xlarge instances.

The authors, who are AWS staff, published the post and point readers to a reference implementation in the aws-do-eks project, which includes steps for prerequisites, cluster creation, weight downloads, deployment, testing, benchmarking, and cleanup. They also suggest using NVIDIA's aiperf tool and concurrency sweeps to measure latency and throughput so that teams can plan capacity. The article presents these steps as a way for customers to start using the model in their own accounts and mentions upcoming AWS workshops on inference on EKS. It does not report any pricing, availability dates beyond the publication date, or further announcements.

Articles.Title: Accelerate agentic AI with NVIDIA Nemotron models on Amazon EKS and SageMaker HyperPod EKS

stories.Headline: Microsoft Positioned to Sustain Elevated AI Spending Without Compromising Finances, Truist Says
stories.Summary:
Microsoft's strong balance sheet and cash flow position it to keep up heavy spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure without straining its finances, according to Truist Securities, which made the argument in a client note. The brokerage's view followed Microsoft's fiscal first-quarter earnings call on Wednesday, when Chief Financial Officer Amy Hood said the company still expects to be free cash flow positive in fiscal 2027. Microsoft reported free cash flow of $18.6 billion for the September quarter. Its shares were up 4.1% in premarket trading on Thursday and have risen 9.8% so far this year.

Hood also said Microsoft now expects capital expenditures of about $170 billion in calendar 2026, down from a previous projection of $175 billion. First-quarter capital spending came in at $45.2 billion, below the company's expectation of more than $50 billion, because some third-party capacity deliveries were pushed into the second half. Expenditures for the current three-month period are forecast to exceed $50 billion. Hood told analysts the company believes each dollar of capital spending can support more revenue and higher returns over time as it improves the efficiency of its infrastructure. Azure, Microsoft's cloud computing unit, saw revenue rise 48% to $33.17 billion in the quarter, and the company expects Azure growth of 49% to 50% in constant currency this quarter.

Truist said Microsoft's financial flexibility lets it sustain elevated investment without materially weakening its position, a point it framed as increasingly important as investors examine the returns on AI spending by large technology companies. The firm contrasted Microsoft with Alphabet, which reported negative free cash flow of $9.07 billion in its third quarter as capital expenditures more than doubled to $51.36 billion, and with Meta Platforms, which reported negative free cash flow of $2.12 billion for the September quarter. Truist also said infrastructure availability remains the main constraint on Azure growth, since customer demand continues to outpace supply. The firm raised its price target on Microsoft to $630 from $600 and kept its buy rating on the stock.

Articles.Title: Microsoft Positioned to Sustain Elevated AI Spending Without Compromising Finances, Truist Says

stories.Headline: How does Meta’s Muse fare against other free AI tools; what precautions should users take?
stories.Summary:
Meta's Muse, an AI agent designed for the mainstream consumer market, became available to users in Singapore on Oct 28, 2026, through the Apple App Store and Google Play Store. It had already launched in the United States and Canada on Sept 8 and in Japan on Oct 23, and it passed 10 million downloads within 40 days of its debut. Within hours of its Singapore launch, it became the most downloaded free app on the Apple App Store there. The Straits Times ran a test comparing it with other free AI tools, and it found Muse was able to do more than the rest. Users must give Muse permission to access data in apps such as Gmail, Instagram and Calendar before it can act on their behalf.

In the test, drafting and sending an email could be done by all four tools, but only Muse could check real-time prescription availability for coloured contact lenses and complete a purchase. When asked to plan a night out, Muse pulled live showtimes, checked seat availability and calculated group ticket prices, while Gemini gave inaccurate show timings and contact lens availability. Muse also acted without being asked, sending an unprompted reminder about a digital arrival card and visa application after spotting an upcoming overseas trip in the calendar. Muse is free with a weekly usage limit, and paid plans cost between $22 and $139 for more usage. The autonomous features of ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini are mostly locked behind paid plans.

Singapore users will be able to connect Muse progressively to apps including Singapore Airlines, Shopee, Lazada, Grab, ShopBack, Agoda, Trip.com and Klook, so it can compare prices, order groceries and book travel. Payments are routed through the third-party wallet Link by Stripe, which generates a unique one-time card number for each purchase so real card details stay private. Yifan Jia, founder of AI safety testing firm AIDX Tech, warned of prompt injection, where hidden instructions in emails or websites could trick an agent into leaking documents, and of automation bias, where users stop checking what agents do. Jia said providers carry a particular responsibility because most consumers are unlikely to adjust security settings, and that the onus is on them to build safety in by default. April Chin, co-chief executive of Resaro, another AI safety testing firm, said users should connect one app at a time and hold off on banking and health data until the agent's scope is clear.

Both experts advised users to grant only the access each task needs and to prefer read-only access, which stops agents from sending messages, changing files or making purchases. Chin urged users to review activity logs regularly and revoke unneeded access, while Jia said actions that cannot be undone, such as payments and outgoing messages, should need human approval. Jia also advised against sharing passwords, Singpass credentials, NRIC numbers or financial information unnecessarily. Chin said personal agents should not be linked to work email or documents without management approval, since this creates a blind spot for IT and security teams. Jia added that employers should set clear AI usage policies, control access, monitor use and provide approved tools, because staff will use these tools with or without a policy.

Articles.Title: How does Meta’s Muse fare against other free AI tools; what precautions should users take?

stories.Headline: Artistic possibilities expanding with AI, ‘2026 Art Korea Lab AI-Convergence Festival’ to be held November 4~8 in Seongsu·Gwanghwamun
stories.Summary:
The 2026 Art Korea Lab AI-Convergence Festival will be held for five days, from November 4 to 8, at Space S-50 in Seongsu-dong, Seoul, and at Art Korea Lab in Jongno-gu. Organized by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism and the Arts Management Support Center, its theme is "Moment Opens Memory." The festival examines the artistic possibilities that open up as the human body and senses meet artificial intelligence technologies. The article was published on October 28, 2026, and the event is open to all.

The program combines conferences, exhibitions, performances, pitching sessions, and participatory activities featuring artists and experts from Korea and abroad.
